international.title: UK-EU deal to confirm ‘Farage penalty’ clause if Britain walks away – UK politics live
international.summary: The Conservatives say the new deal barely contains savings for UK citizens We should get the latest Mandelson documents (see 9.17am ) around lunchtime. The Commons authorities have announced there will be two ministerial statements today. At around 11.30pm Polly Billington, an energy minister, will make a statement about the latest price cap announced by Ofgem yesterday. And, about an hour later, Dan Jarvis, the security minister, will make a statement described as an “update on the government response to the Peter Mandelson humble address motion”. Sam Coates from Sky News has posted this on social media about what the new documents might reveal. In today’s Mandelson files, I’m expecting a revealing look into the desperate attempts by the civil service to manage the political curveball they’d been thrown by Keir Starmer and Morgan McSweeny. Mandelson was a political appointment, pretty much forced through by No 10 with nobody listening to the warnings. Keir Starmer’s team were not interested in the problems with this appointment. Analysis by the Conservatives of the government’s own estimates shows that the savings from the sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) deal will amount to just pennies on everyday essentials, despite Andy Burnham promising the deal would bring down food prices. Beef prices have risen by 27.8 per cent since Labour took office, adding £1.22 to a pack of beef mince. Yet the government’s SPS deal would save shoppers just over 1p on a £5.60 pack.
